audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Trundle all seven stages — content win is ["Trundle" x7] and every phases[].side reads Trundle — while Trundle actually loses this lane at 48.69% over 306 games. The whys underneath disagree with their own labels in the other direction: whys[2] "the matchup becomes skill-based", whys[5] "the edge depends on who lands the cleaner engage", whys[6] "it is a genuine skill contest".
audit.why: A seven-for-seven sweep printed over a losing win rate is the most misleading chart shape on the page — it tells a player he cannot lose a lane he loses more often than he wins. Three of the seven whys already describe the stage as even, and the two that describe Trundle winning (levels 1 and 2, plus the level-6 Subjugate window) are the ones the kit supports: Nimbus Strike does not exist until level 3, so before that Wukong has no way out of a Frozen Domain.
audit.corrected: Trundle at levels 1, 2 and 6; Skill at level 3, levels 4-5, first item and two-plus items.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3], `late` and whys[6] all treat Cyclone as the late-game threat with no cooldown attached, and spikes[1] describes the level-6 spike purely as an armour drain.
audit.why: Cyclone is 130/110/90 seconds against Subjugate's 120/100/80 — at rank 1 Trundle's ultimate is back ten seconds sooner, which is the whole reason to take the duel after Wukong spends his. And the level-6 spike is bigger than the page says: Subjugate takes a fifth of his maximum health as damage and heals Trundle for the same amount on top of the 40% resist steal. Stone Skin also stacks armour while he fights, so the pool R draws from grows a few seconds into the exchange rather than being fixed at first contact.
audit.corrected: Cyclone 130s at rank 1 against Subjugate's 120s. Stone Skin stacks armour during the fight, so the resist steal is biggest a few seconds in.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nimbus Strike is labelled Wukong's escape in four fields — breakdown.cooldowns "His escape. Punish the cooldown", dosFull[0].d, report[5].t, and the whole tldr/winCon/loading axis built on "Track Nimbus Strike".
audit.why: Nimbus Strike is a 650-range dash TO a targeted enemy — it is how he gets in, not how he gets out. The escape is Warrior Trickster: he turns Invisible, dashes, and leaves a clone behind. Those two abilities have very different cooldowns, 10/9.25/8.5/7.75/7 against 22/21/20/19/18, so a Trundle tracking the wrong one is waiting on a ten-second cooldown while the twenty-two-second one is the window that actually matters. The page's own clone advice is right and is attached to the wrong ability.
audit.corrected: Warrior Trickster (22s at rank 1) is the escape; Nimbus Strike (10s at rank 1) is the engage.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0], whys[0] and wants.you[1] say Chomp slows Wukong's attack speed. `early` says spending Pillar of Ice on the clone costs you "your only hard repositioning tool for ten seconds". `mid` says Subjugate steals "half his armor and MR".
audit.why: Chomp saps Attack Damage and slows movement — no attack-speed component. Pillar of Ice is 21 seconds at rank 1, not ten, which more than doubles the real cost of wasting it on a decoy and is exactly the kind of number that changes whether a player risks it. And Subjugate takes 40%, not half.
audit.corrected: Chomp: AD sap and a movement slow. Pillar of Ice: 21s at rank 1. Subjugate: 40%.

audit.whatIsWrong: Crushing Blow is described only as "his Q armor-shred" and its two other properties are never stated.
audit.why: Riot's text gives Crushing Blow bonus ATTACK RANGE as well as the armour reduction, scaling 250/275/300/325/350 — which means from rank 3 onward he out-ranges Chomp's 300 with an empowered attack. It is also an auto-attack reset, the burst tell _missing-interactions.json flags for this matchup, so his damage arrives on the wind-up rather than on a cast animation. Both change where a Trundle stands during a trade.
audit.corrected: Crushing Blow (8s at rank 1): auto-reset, armour shred, and bonus range out to 350 — past Chomp's 300.

audit.whatIsWrong: `late` says a Cyclone landed inside Frozen Domain "interrupts your healing and AS buff for the knockup duration".
audit.why: The knockup stops Trundle acting — no autos, no Chomp — and can move him off the zone, but Frozen Domain's healing and attack speed are properties of standing on the zone and are not themselves interrupted by a displacement. Overstating what the knockup removes makes it read as a hard counter to the W rather than as a reset on the trade, which is what it actually is.
audit.corrected: Cyclone's knockup stops your autos and your Chomp mid-pattern and hands him the reset.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown number appears in either layer, and breakdown.cooldowns names two abilities with no figures.
audit.why: Crushing Blow 8/7.5/7/6.5/6s, Warrior Trickster 22/21/20/19/18s, Nimbus Strike 10/9.25/8.5/7.75/7s, Cyclone 130/110/90s, against Chomp's flat 3.5s and Pillar of Ice's 21s. The rule that falls out is specific: bait Warrior Trickster and you own the next twenty-two seconds, which is longer than any other window in the matchup.
audit.corrected: Figures added to breakdown.cooldowns, phases[2], phases[4], report[5], dosFull[0], spikes, early, mid, late and three whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8] buys Executioner's Calling on the first back "— cuts his healing".
audit.why: No Wukong ability carries a heal flag and _missing-interactions.json raises no needs-antiheal for this matchup; Stone Skin is health regeneration during a fight, not a heal that Grievous Wounds meaningfully answers. The one real healing source is Sundered Sky, which the page itself lists as an optional first item — so the buy is conditional, not automatic, and 800 gold spent on it against a Black Cleaver Wukong is 800 gold wasted.
audit.corrected: Executioner's Calling only if he buys Sundered Sky.

audit.why: No suspectNames were raised for this matchup and the ability names in use are correct. The clone-baiting advice is genuinely good and I kept all of it — only its cooldown and its ability attribution needed fixing.

edits.before: At level 1, immediately max Q and force a Chomp trade: the AD steal and attack speed slow tilt the 2-auto exchange in your favor before Wukong can establish any pattern. At level 2, if you pick up W, plant Frozen Domain under the first trade and he has nothing at this point to escape it — he is melee, has no dash until E, and loses any trade that lasts more than three seconds. The critical early habit is watching for his W clone: do not blow your Pillar of Ice (E) on the clone or you lose your only hard repositioning tool for ten seconds, letting him trade back cleanly. Chomp him, not the decoy.
edits.after: At level 1, max Q and force a Chomp trade: the AD sap tilts the two-auto exchange in your favour before Wukong establishes any pattern. At level 2 plant Frozen Domain under the first trade — he has nothing to leave it with, because Nimbus Strike arrives at 3 and Warrior Trickster is 22 seconds at rank 1. The critical early habit is watching for the clone: do not spend Pillar of Ice on it, because that is 21 seconds at rank 1 and it is your only hard repositioning tool. The real Wukong is the one walking toward you; the clone stands and swings.

edits.before: Once Wukong hits level 3 with Q plus E plus W he becomes a genuine threat — his E dash gives him a real engage, his Q shreds your armor, and his W clone can bait your reaction. Play every extended trade inside Frozen Domain and keep Pillar off cooldown so you can cut off his clone-escape route when he tries to disengage. At level 6, immediately look for the Subjugate all-in: activate R first hit into him as he engages, stealing half his armor and MR instantly, then stand your ground in Frozen Domain and let Chomp's compound AD steal do the rest — he has no clean way to burst you through the resistance you just borrowed from him. Respect his R Cyclone timing: if you see him standing still or spinning up, Pillar can cut off his knockup path rather than being used reactively.
edits.after: Once Wukong hits level 3 with Q, W and E he becomes a genuine threat — Nimbus Strike is a 650-range dash onto you every 10 seconds at rank 1, Crushing Blow shreds your armour and gains attack range out to 350, and Warrior Trickster leaves a clone while he turns Invisible. Play every extended trade inside Frozen Domain and hold Pillar of Ice for the real body. At 6 look for the Subjugate all-in: 40% of his armour and MR plus a fifth of his max health, healing you the same and doubling over 4 seconds — and because Stone Skin stacks armour while he fights, the pool you draw from is biggest a few seconds in, not at first contact. Cyclone is 130s at rank 1, ten seconds longer than your own ultimate: once he spends it, the next duel in the side lane is yours to take.

edits.before: By the two-item mark Wukong has closed the durability gap considerably — his armor itemization is genuinely annoying because it gives him resistances to stack, but Subjugate recycles those right back onto you, so stay disciplined about ult timing in every prolonged skirmish. His R knockup mid-spin is the biggest threat in late-game side-lane duels: if he gets the Cyclone off inside your Frozen Domain it interrupts your healing and AS buff for the knockup duration, effectively resetting the trade in his favor. Save Pillar to cut off his spin path or body-block his exit — do not use it as an opener and waste it on his clone.
edits.after: By the two-item mark Wukong has closed the durability gap — his armour build is genuinely annoying, but Subjugate recycles 40% of it straight back onto you and takes a fifth of his health with it, so stay disciplined about ultimate timing in every skirmish. Cyclone is the biggest threat in a side-lane duel: the knockup stops your autos and your Chomp mid-pattern and hands him the reset. At 130 seconds at rank 1 it is slower than your own 120, so the duel to take is the one after he spends it. Save Pillar of Ice to cut his exit or body-block the spin — never as an opener, and never on the clone.

notes: Chart was Trundle 7/7 over a 48.69% win rate — the worst chart-versus-data mismatch in my slice, and the opposite direction to the Tryndamere/Volibear/Warwick cases where Trundle was given zero stages in lanes he wins. Both failure modes appear in the same file, so the charts look generated independently of both the data and the paragraphs. Second finding: Nimbus Strike is called Wukong's escape in four fields including the tldr, winCon and loading screen; the escape is Warrior Trickster at 22s, and tracking the 10-second ability instead of the 22-second one is a real cost. Anti-heal was marked Medium rather than High because Sundered Sky genuinely heals and the page lists it as a possible Wukong item — the buy is conditional rather than wrong.
